citation: Schmittner MD, Faulhaber J, Kemler B, Koenen W, Thumfart JO, Weiss C, Neumaier M, Beck GC. Influence of high dose tumescent local anaesthesia with prilocaine on systemic interleukin (IL)-6, IL-8 and tumour necrosis factor-α. J Eur Acad Dermatol Venereol 2010;24(12):1400–1405
text_quality: ok — 6 PDF pages with a text layer; Greek letters extracted as Latin ('TNF-a', 'lg ⁄ mL'); Table 2 readable in the layout view; Figures 1–3 plot the same values as Table 2. Internal inconsistency in the paper: 20 melanoma patients in Results and Table 1, but a melanoma subgroup of n = 22 in 'Special clinical courses'.
design: Prospective, single-centre, observational before-after cohort without a control group (each patient's pre-infiltration blood sample is the reference), plus an in-vitro whole-blood experiment with cycloheximide. Registered as ISRCTN 19821978; ethics vote 2007-258N-MA. The paper has no limitations paragraph.
population: 30 adults (16 men, 14 women; mean age 54.9 years, range 18–85; ASA I–III) having in-house dermatological surgery for large resections under tumescent local anaesthesia: 20 malignant melanoma, 8 acne inversa, 2 other malignant skin tumours (Table 1). 42 patients had surgery under tumescent anaesthesia in the period; 8 did not meet the inclusion criteria and 4 declined. Exclusions: prilocaine allergy, ASA IV–VI, pregnancy.
n: 30, one group (a melanoma subgroup was also analysed separately; the paper gives it as n = 22 although Table 1 lists 20 melanoma patients)
setting: University Medical Center Mannheim (Heidelberg University), Germany — anaesthesiology, dermatology, clinical chemistry and statistics departments; January–September 2008; oral midazolam premedication, optional propofol sedation, oxygen by face mask, ECG/blood pressure/oxygen saturation monitoring.
intervention: Tumescent local anaesthesia: a dilute prilocaine-with-epinephrine solution in balanced crystalloid, infused subcutaneously by pump for large resections, at high total prilocaine doses [dose figure omitted]; a single session.
comparator: None. No group without prilocaine and none without surgery, so the rise in IL-6 and CRP cannot be separated from the effect of the surgery itself (the authors attribute it to prilocaine-induced methaemoglobin).
duration: Single procedure; venous blood before infiltration and at 1, 2, 4, 12, 24, 48 and 72 h.
outcomes: Serum IL-6, IL-8 and TNF-α (the stated aim); methaemoglobin (blood-gas analyser, haemolysed venous blood) at every time point; serum prilocaine (LC-MS); CRP, LDH, CK, PCT, haemoglobin; clinical symptoms; correlations between applied dose, serum prilocaine, methaemoglobin and cytokines; in-vitro IL-6 production by whole blood stimulated with prilocaine or o-toluidine, with and without cycloheximide.

key_results.quote: This prospective, single-centre, observational study was performed according to the guidelines of the Ethic Commission II, Faculty for Clinical Medicine Mannheim, Germany

The present prospective study examines the influence of prilocaine-induced MHb on serum levels of interleukin (IL)-6, IL-8 and tumour necrosis factor (TNF)-a up to 72 h after application of TLA with prilocaine in doses higher than [dose figure omitted] in extended dermatological surgery and investigates clinical symptoms.
Blood samples were drawn before application of TLA solution (basal) as well as 1, 2, 4, 12, 24, 48 and 72 h.

Basal MHb serum levels (Fig. 2) were [dose figure omitted]. The level increased to [dose figure omitted] after 1 h, to [dose figure omitted] after 2 h, to [dose figure omitted] after 4 h with a peak of [dose figure omitted] 12 h after TLA
MHb serum levels decreased rapidly to [dose figure omitted] after 24 h and to [dose figure omitted] after 48 h (P < 0.0001 for MHb serum level changes over time; ANOVA).
Overall, an MHb concentration [dose figure omitted] was measured in three patients
No clinical symptoms were observed and no specific therapy was indicated.

Four hours after TLA, one 18-year-old female patient suffering from a malignant melanoma developed mild symptoms of cyanosis and hyperventilation at a maximum MHb concentration of [dose figure omitted].
IL-6 concentration reached a peak maximum of … (P < 0.001) 12 h after TLA.
Serum levels of IL-8 and TNF-a serum did not change significantly in the chronological sequence compared with baseline levels
Furthermore, no statistically significant correlation between the applied doses of prilocaine and MHb or prilocaine serum levels and IL-6, IL-8 or TNF-a concentrations could be detected.
A CRP peak maximum of … was reached at 48 h (P < 0.0001 compared with basal levels).
No correlation between MHb and IL-6 concentration was found at any time.
Interleukin-6 synthesis was completely inhibited under simultaneous CX and prilocaine stimulation, indicating the de novo synthesis of this chemokine by immunmodulatory cells (data not shown).
This clinical study demonstrates for the first time that high doses of prilocaine induce MHb generation and the enhanced release of IL-6, but not of IL-8 or TNF-a in vivo.
Current publications recommend a dose limitation of [dose figure omitted].8
As a result of possible and unpredictable high MHb concentrations, TLA can only be recommended with prilocaine in doses of [dose figure omitted].8

author_limitations.quote: The analysis of PCT was stopped after 20 patients as no correlation was found.

Further investigations are now necessary to explain the difference in cytokine production on molecular level and to improve the development of TLA solutions to reach an adequate analgesia and to minimize side-effects, in extended dermatological resections.
